scenes.line1: Can Go functions work with any type?
scenes.say: Can Go functions work with any type? How do generics fit into this?

scenes.label: Generics
scenes.sub: Type parameters let code work with any type.
scenes.say: Go version one point eighteen introduced generics. Type parameters let your code work with any type.
Here's a generic sum function. The type parameter T can be int or float sixty-four. This keeps your code reusable and type safe.

scenes.label: Constraints
scenes.say: Keep your constraints simple for readability. Overcomplicating them makes code harder to maintain.

scenes.question: Can generics detect embedded types?
scenes.right: No, Go generics can't directly detect embedded types. Use method sets or marker interfaces instead.
scenes.say: Here's a common interview trap. Can generics detect embedded types? No, Go generics can't do this directly. Use method sets or marker interfaces instead.
